editorial.headline: Photography Retail: Nationally Open, Barred for PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 47731 covers the retail sale of cameras, projection and sound equipment—open to full foreign ownership nationally, yet barred from PMA registration in Bali under its moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 47731 is the retail activity for photographic equipment and its supporting apparatus. Its scope embraces still cameras and cinematographic cameras, cinematographic projectors, sound-recording and sound-reproduction equipment, image projectors and overhead projectors. It also reaches photographic flash apparatus, camera frames and bodies, image-projector equipment, and film-cassette transfer equipment. The through-line is clear: this is an activity defined by selling the equipment and accessories used to capture, record, reproduce or project images and sound. The formal title is broad enough to include both the core devices and the operational kit around them.

The registration audience is therefore a business undertaking this particular form of retail trade, rather than an abstract technology label. The record opens it to Micro, Small, Medium and Large enterprises, so the code is not confined to one company size. That breadth matters as a statement of scale, not as a promise about a business model: the scope remains the listed photographic, projection, recording and related equipment. A registrant should keep the activity description anchored in that inventory, because it supplies the code’s own boundary.

At national level, the ownership position is unambiguous. The activity is open to foreign investment, and the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In ordinary terms, the national record permits complete foreign ownership of the company carrying out this retail activity. The legal reference given is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national openness is significant, but it is not the end of the location question; the Bali record brings a distinct provincial result that must be read on its own terms.

For Bali, the answer for a PMA registration is a block, not a qualification: a foreigner cannot register this activity there today. The record marks its Bali status as BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO and attributes the outcome to the Bali moratorium. In the OSS assessment cited, every scope at the Large scale falls in Low or Medium-Low risk. Bali’s island-wide, permanent rule blocks all KBLI in those risk classes for PMA, and the cited moratorium is identified with May 2026. Nationally, 100% foreign ownership is allowed; in Bali, the moratorium prevents PMA registration of this activity.
